title: Build an actionable Next.js latency and reliability SLO
businessContext: The only metric is next build duration, yet users report slow navigation and intermittent action failures.
problemStatement: Design the system for p95 route interaction under 1 second; 99.9% successful authenticated operations. Produce the component/data-flow diagram, request and mutation contracts, cache/trust boundaries, capacity assumptions, failure recovery and rollout gates. State which decisions change between Next.js 15 and 16 instead of using a framework API as a substitute for an architectural guarantee.
constraints: Measure user-visible and server dependency boundaries.
candidateTasks: Draw components and annotate ownership of data, identity, caches and durable work.
Specify contracts/schema and quantify the capacity/freshness assumptions.
Walk through the failure scenario and design measurable acceptance tests.
Compare the reference decisions and answer the changed-requirement interview prompt.

systemDesignReqs.scale: p95 route interaction under 1 second; 99.9% successful authenticated operations
functional: Measure user-visible and server dependency boundaries.
nonFunctional: State an explicit latency, freshness and recovery budget rather than inventing guarantees.
Keep actor/tenant isolation and failure ownership observable.
assumptions: A patched App Router deployment; platform-specific infrastructure support must be verified.
Next.js version and Cache Components configuration are explicit design inputs.

hints: Define successful operations, excluded conditions and a measurement window before choosing an error budget.

A global average can hide a tenant-specific outage or a cold-cache tail. Preserve bounded-cardinality cohorts and inspect distributions; do not attach arbitrary user emails or full URLs as unbounded metric labels.
alternativeApproaches: Unbounded logs and high-cardinality metrics can create cost, privacy and reliability problems. Instrument a causal model with useful sampling and retention, and measure the telemetry pipeline’s own failure behavior.
commonMistakes: Claiming a cache API provides transactions, durable delivery or cross-region consistency.
Omitting authorization, recovery budgets or evidence from an otherwise attractive component diagram.

verification: Inject latency separately into auth, database and client code.
Confirm an alert points to useful diagnostic evidence and a bounded mitigation.
Compare cold/warm and direct/client navigation measurements without combining unlike events.
nextjsPractice.next15: Use patched Next.js 15 and the router family named by the file path. Await request APIs where the App Router contract requires it; validate behavior in a production build.
nextjsPractice.next16: Applies to Next.js 16.4.5. Cache Components is disabled unless the exercise explicitly enables it. The simulator itself remains on 16.4.3.
